items.name: Anchor Hocking glassware (and Pyrex, now Lancaster OH)
items.what: Anchor Hocking glass bakeware, storage, and drinkware are made in Lancaster, Ohio, and Pyrex production has moved there too after the USW-represented Charleroi, Pennsylvania plant closed in April 2025.
items.caveats: Northshore AFL-CIO lists Anchor Hocking as USW, but confirm the current Lancaster contract. Pyrex bakeware sold in 2025 and 2026 could be either Lancaster-made or imported, so check the marking. The old Charleroi Pyrex plant, which was USW Local 53G, is gone.

items.name: Fiesta dinnerware (Fiesta Tableware Co., formerly Homer Laughlin)
items.what: Fiesta ceramic dinnerware, made by Fiesta Tableware Company, formerly Homer Laughlin, is made in Newell, West Virginia.
items.caveats: The USW affiliation comes from the Northshore AFL-CIO union-made list. Homer Laughlin's foodservice lines were sold to Steelite in 2020, but Fiesta Tableware kept the Newell plant.

items.name: Cutco cutlery and kitchen tools
items.what: Cutco kitchen knives, shears, and utensils are all made in Olean, New York.
items.caveats: Some non-knife accessories and cookware are made in Mexico or China. Cutco is sold mainly through Vector Marketing's direct sales, plus a few company stores.

items.name: Libbey glassware - Toledo, Ohio
items.what: Libbey drinking glasses and tumblers are made at the glass plant in Toledo, Ohio.
items.caveats: The union status here is based on Toledo's long history as a USW glassworkers town, but we couldn't find a current union-list citation for it. Libbey also makes glassware in Monterrey, Mexico, Portugal, and the Netherlands, so look for 'Made in USA' on the box.

items.name: Interior Crafts furniture - Chicago
items.what: Interior Crafts hand-built upholstered and case furniture is made by about 70 USW members in Chicago, Illinois, one of the last unionized furniture makers left in the country.
items.caveats: This sells through trade and designer showrooms, with custom pricing.

items.name: La-Z-Boy recliners - Dayton, Tennessee plant
items.what: La-Z-Boy recliners and sofas from the Dayton, Tennessee plant are covered by a union agreement, according to local press, with about 1,800 workers there.
items.union: Union present at Dayton TN (union name not confirmed in accessible sources)
items.caveats: Dayton, Tennessee is the only La-Z-Boy plant reported to have a union agreement. The Neosho, Missouri and Siloam Springs, Arkansas plants, plus cut-and-sew work in Ramos Arizpe, Mexico, are not union. There's no way to tell which plant made a given piece at retail without asking.

items.name: Serta / Sealy mattresses (select plants)
items.what: Serta and Sealy mattresses from certain regional plants are listed by the Northshore AFL-CIO as CWA (Communications Workers of America) made, and Serta has historically had contracts with Carpenters and Lumber and Sawmill Workers locals.
items.union: CWA (per Northshore AFL-CIO list); other plants USW/Teamsters/Carpenters
items.caveats: Mattresses are built regionally, so union status varies plant by plant, and several Serta Simmons plants closed in 2023 and 2024. Ask the retailer which plant made the specific unit. Tempur-Pedic, owned by Tempur Sealy, is not confirmed union at any plant.

items.name: Kohler plumbing fixtures, faucets and engines - Kohler, Wisconsin
items.what: Kohler cast-iron and vitreous china bath and toilet fixtures, faucets, and small engines are built at the Village of Kohler and Town of Mosel, Wisconsin plants, under a five-year UAW contract running from 2023 to 2028.
items.caveats: Kohler also makes fixtures in Spartanburg, South Carolina, Brownsville and Searcy, Arkansas, Huntsville, Alabama, Mexico, China, and India, and Sterling and many Kohler faucets are imported. Look for 'Made in Kohler, WI' stamped on cast iron pieces.

brand: kohler plumbing fixtures, faucets and engines

items.name: BrassCraft (Masco) plumbing parts and supplies
items.what: BrassCraft supply lines, valves, and plumbing parts are handled at Masco's BrassCraft operation in Michigan.
items.caveats: The 2019 UAW guide lists this as packaging and handling for plumbing parts and supplies, and much of what BrassCraft sells is actually imported and just packaged domestically.

items.name: Mueller Industries brass stock
items.what: Mueller Industries makes brass rod and stock, used to manufacture plumbing fittings, at a plant in Michigan.
items.caveats: Only this brass-stock plant appears in the UAW guide. Mueller's copper tube and fittings plants, in places like Fulton, Mississippi and Covington, Tennessee, are not confirmed union.

items.name: Threaded Products Co. household plumbing fittings
items.what: Threaded Products Co. makes household plumbing fittings with members of UAW Local 9699, part of UAW Region 1 in Michigan.
items.caveats: This is a small supplier to other manufacturers, with no direct-to-consumer buying option.

items.name: Reed Manufacturing plumbing tools - Erie, PA
items.what: Reed Manufacturing pipe wrenches, cutters, threaders, and other plumbing equipment are made in Erie, Pennsylvania.
items.caveats: This is a professional plumbing tool line sold through supply houses.

items.name: Andersen / EMCO storm doors - Des Moines, Iowa
items.what: Andersen-branded storm doors sold at Home Depot, actually made by EMCO, are built in Des Moines, Iowa by members of UAW Local 1672 Unit 1.
items.caveats: The only source for this is the 2019 UAW products guide. We couldn't find any 2020 through 2026 news, contract, or Local 1672 page confirming the EMCO unit still exists, though the Des Moines plant is still running. Check with UAW Region 4 before treating this as current. Only the storm-door plant is union. Andersen's main window plants, in Bayport, Minnesota and Menomonie, Wisconsin, and its Renewal by Andersen line, are not union.

items.name: L.E. Johnson Products door hardware - Elkhart, Indiana
items.what: L.E. Johnson Products pocket-door frames and sliding and bifold door hardware are made in Elkhart, Indiana.

items.name: Johns Manville insulation - Defiance, Ohio
items.what: Johns Manville fiberglass insulation is produced at the Defiance, Ohio plant.
items.caveats: Johns Manville, owned by Berkshire Hathaway, has other plants with mixed union status, some USW represented. Defiance is the one listed by the UAW.

items.name: Hancock Enterprises aluminum gutters and downspouts
items.what: Hancock Enterprises aluminum gutters and downspouts are made in Michigan by members of UAW Local 174.
items.caveats: This is a regional supplier sold through contractors.

brand: hancock enterprises aluminum gutters and downspouts

items.name: Central Aluminum patio enclosures
items.what: Central Aluminum patio enclosures and sunroom components are made in Ohio by members of UAW Local 1588.
items.caveats: This is a regional product sold through the contractor channel.

items.name: Air Conditioning Products Co. dampers and wall shutters
items.what: Air Conditioning Products Co. makes HVAC dampers and exhaust wall shutters in Michigan.

brand: air conditioning products . dampers and wall shutters

items.name: Warminster Fiberglass
items.what: Warminster Fiberglass makes fiberglass tanks and enclosures in Southampton, Pennsylvania.
items.caveats: These are mostly industrial and municipal products with limited relevance to home shoppers.

items.name: Sheboygan Paint Company
items.what: Sheboygan Paint Company makes industrial and architectural coatings in Sheboygan, Wisconsin, and is listed in the UAW-made product directory.
items.caveats: This is mostly industrial and OEM coatings, with limited retail availability.

items.name: Sherwin-Williams paint (select US plants)
items.what: Sherwin-Williams architectural paints are made at US plants and appear on the Northshore AFL-CIO union-made list, though that list doesn't name which union.
items.union: Plant-dependent (Teamsters/USW/IUOE at some plants) - not confirmed
items.caveats: This appears on a union-affiliated gift list, but that list itself says it wasn't independently verified. Sherwin-Williams retail stores are not union. Treat this as US-made with uncertain union status.

items.name: U.S. Steel (Nippon Steel) - Gary Works, Mon Valley, Granite City
items.what: US Steel, now owned by Nippon Steel, makes flat-rolled, plate, tin, and structural steel at integrated mills represented by USW: Gary Works in Indiana (Local 1014), Mon Valley Works in Pennsylvania (Edgar Thomson, Irvin, and Clairton plants), and Granite City, Illinois (Local 1899).
items.caveats: Big River Steel in Osceola, Arkansas is not union. The Nippon Steel acquisition closed in June 2025, and the USW contract stayed in force. Consumers usually see this steel indirectly, in things like appliances, framing, and roofing.

items.name: Cleveland-Cliffs steel - Burns Harbor, Indiana Harbor, Cleveland, Middletown, Dearborn
items.what: Cleveland-Cliffs, North America's largest flat-rolled steel producer, makes sheet, plate, stainless, and electrical steel at former ArcelorMittal and AK Steel mills, represented by USW, including Local 1010 at Indiana Harbor and Local 6787 at Burns Harbor.
items.caveats: Some of the former AK Steel plants are represented by IAM or UAW instead of USW. Cliffs idled or slowed several plants in 2025. Like other steel, this is an indirect consumer product.

items.name: USG gypsum wallboard (Sheetrock) - select plants
items.what: USG's Sheetrock brand gypsum wallboard and joint compound come from a mix of union plants. Gypsum workers were historically organized by the United Cement, Lime and Gypsum Workers, which merged into the Boilermakers in 1984, and USW represents workers at other USG plants.
items.union: Boilermakers (ex-Cement, Lime & Gypsum Workers) / USW - plant-dependent
items.caveats: Not every USG plant is union, and the board you buy at a big-box store could be from any regional plant. We couldn't find a current union-made list that names USG specifically, so ask the lumber yard which plant supplied the load.

items.name: Armstrong World Industries ceilings / AHF (Armstrong) flooring - Lancaster, PA
items.what: Armstrong mineral-fiber ceiling tiles come from Armstrong World Industries plants in Lancaster and Marietta, Pennsylvania, and Armstrong-brand resilient flooring is now made by AHF Products, also in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. The Northshore AFL-CIO list attributes Armstrong to IBEW and UAW.
items.union: IBEW / UAW per Northshore AFL-CIO list; USW at Lancaster plants historically
items.caveats: Armstrong Flooring went bankrupt in 2022, and the flooring brand is now owned by AHF Products, so its plant union status should be checked again. The ceiling tile business, Armstrong World Industries, is a separate company from the flooring business.

items.name: Eaton electrical products (IBEW-made lines)
items.what: Eaton, sold under the Cutler-Hammer name for some products, makes circuit breakers, load centers, and other electrical products that IBEW's manufacturing department cites as IBEW-made brand examples.
items.caveats: IBEW names Eaton as an IBEW-made brand but doesn't say which plants. Many Eaton residential breakers are actually made in Mexico or Puerto Rico, so check the 'Made in USA' marking before buying.

items.name: GE Profile refrigerators and GE washing machines (IBEW-listed)
items.what: The Northshore AFL-CIO union-made list separately credits GE Profile refrigerators and GE washing machines to IBEW members, in addition to the IUE-CWA (International Union of Electronic Workers-Communications Workers of America) workers at the Louisville plant.
items.caveats: This overlaps with the main Louisville, Kentucky GE Appliances entry, and the IBEW credit may reflect component plants rather than final assembly. Buy models built in Louisville.

brand: ge profile refrigerators and ge washing machines

items.name: Weyerhaeuser lumber and engineered wood (Pacific Northwest mills)
items.what: Weyerhaeuser dimensional lumber, plywood, OSB, and TJI engineered wood come from mills in Oregon and Washington, represented by IAM Woodworkers locals and USW wood-products locals.
items.caveats: Weyerhaeuser's southern US mills are mostly not union, while its Canadian mills are USW. There's no way to tell union status once the lumber reaches the yard.

items.name: Owens Corning insulation and shingles (select plants)
items.what: Owens Corning PINK fiberglass insulation and asphalt shingles come from a mix of plants, with USW representing workers at several insulation and roofing locations including Kansas City, Kansas and Newark, Ohio.
items.caveats: We couldn't find one consolidated union-made citation for Owens Corning, and several of its plants, especially newer ones in the South, are not union. Check the plant code on the bundle.

items.name: Thermador appliances (Boilermakers-listed)
items.what: The Northshore AFL-CIO union-made gift list attributes Thermador appliances to the Boilermakers union.
items.caveats: Thermador is owned by BSH, and its main US plant, in New Bern, North Carolina, isn't known to be union. This attribution likely dates back to older production near Los Angeles, so treat it with skepticism.

items.name: Hoover vacuums (IBEW-listed, historical)
items.what: Hoover vacuums appear on the Northshore AFL-CIO union-made list as IBEW-made.
items.caveats: This is outdated. Hoover's North Canton, Ohio plant closed in 2007, and current Hoover vacuums, made by TTI, are imported. This entry is included only to flag that old assumption as wrong.

items.name: Walbro lawn & garden home products / Whirltronics mower blades
items.what: Walbro fuel tanks and lawn-and-garden home products come from UAW Local 9699 Unit 6, and Whirltronics lawnmower blades come from UAW Local 125 Unit 40.
items.caveats: These are parts suppliers to other companies, so you'd encounter them inside other brands' mowers, not as standalone purchases.

items.name: John Deere residential lawn mowers - Horicon, Wisconsin
items.what: John Deere lawn tractors and residential mowers are built in Horicon, Wisconsin by IAM members, also listed by the Wisconsin AFL-CIO.
items.caveats: Some Deere residential mowers, like those from the Greeneville, Tennessee plant, are not union, so check the model's origin.

items.name: Euclid Chemical concrete additives
items.what: Euclid Chemical concrete admixtures and construction chemicals are made in the Cleveland, Ohio area by members of UAW Local 70.
items.caveats: This sells through the contractor and professional channel.

items.name: Frigidaire / White-Westinghouse / Tappan / Gibson / Kelvinator laundry (historical Union Plus listing)
items.what: An older Union Plus union-made appliance guide lists Electrolux's Frigidaire, White-Westinghouse, Tappan, Gibson, and Kelvinator laundry centers, washers, and dryers as IUE-CWA and UAW made.
items.union: IUE-CWA / UAW (historic Webster City IA and St. Cloud MN plants)
items.caveats: This listing is stale. Electrolux closed the UAW-represented Webster City, Iowa laundry plant in 2011 and the IUE-CWA St. Cloud, Minnesota freezer plant in 2019. Current Frigidaire laundry products are made in Mexico, and Electrolux's remaining US plants, in Anderson, South Carolina (fridges), Springfield, Tennessee (ranges), and Kinston, North Carolina (dishwashers), have no confirmed union.

items.name: FairHotel.org (UNITE HERE union hotel finder)
items.what: FairHotel.org is UNITE HERE's searchable directory and mobile app for finding union hotels across the US and Canada. You can search by city to see which properties have UNITE HERE contracts and which are under boycott. Check it before booking any hotel.
items.caveats: Union status is decided property by property, not by hotel chain, so a Hilton in one city can be union while a Hilton in another city isn't. Check the site's boycott list before you book.

items.name: Minneapolis-St. Paul union hotels (UNITE HERE Local 17)
items.what: Hotels covered by UNITE HERE Local 17 in the Twin Cities include the Hilton Minneapolis, JW Marriott Minneapolis at Mall of America, Sheraton Minneapolis Downtown, Royal Sonesta Minneapolis, The Marquette Hotel, Hotel Ivy, Lofton Hotel, Courtyard Minneapolis Downtown, Residence Inn by Marriott, Radisson Blu Mall of America, Renaissance Minneapolis Bloomington, DoubleTree Bloomington, InterContinental St. Paul Riverfront, InterContinental MSP Airport, The Saint Paul Hotel, Delta Hotels Minneapolis Northeast, Best Western Normandy, Holiday Inn Express and Suites, and Kahler Hospitality in Rochester, Minnesota.
items.caveats: This list comes from Local 17's contracts page. Confirm current status on fairhotel.org before booking, since contracts and ownership change.

items.name: Chicago downtown union hotels (UNITE HERE Local 1)
items.what: More than 30 downtown Chicago hotels operate under UNITE HERE Local 1 contracts, including Marriott, Hilton properties like the Palmer House and Hilton Chicago, Hyatt properties like Hyatt Regency Chicago and Hyatt Regency McCormick Place, the W City Center, and The Drake. A 2023 agreement set a $25 an hour minimum for non-tipped workers.
items.caveats: The 2023 contracts were three-year deals expiring in August 2026, so check fairhotel.org for any strike or boycott status. Not every downtown Chicago hotel from these brands is union.

items.name: Las Vegas Strip union casino-resorts (Culinary Union Local 226 / Bartenders Local 165)
items.what: As of 2025, every major Las Vegas Strip casino-resort is union, represented by Culinary Union Local 226 and Bartenders Local 165. That includes all MGM Resorts properties like Bellagio, MGM Grand, Mandalay Bay, Luxor, New York-New York, and Aria, all Caesars Entertainment properties like Caesars Palace, Flamingo, Harrah's, and Paris, Wynn and Encore, plus The Venetian, The Palazzo, and Fontainebleau, which won their first contracts in 2024 and 2025, along with Palms, Golden Nugget, Circus Circus, and Four Seasons. About 60,000 members are covered by a citywide five-year contract from 2023.
items.union: UNITE HERE Culinary Workers Local 226 & Bartenders Local 165
items.caveats: Some restaurants inside these union resorts are run by third-party operators who aren't union. Culinary's UnionEats.org lists more than 360 union restaurants on and near the Strip. Casinos off the Strip and in the suburbs vary.

items.name: New York City union hotels (Hotel & Gaming Trades Council)
items.what: The large majority of full-service Manhattan hotels, including Hilton, Marriott, Hyatt, Sheraton, Westin, Waldorf, and Plaza properties, are covered by the Hotel and Gaming Trades Council's Industry-Wide Agreement. A new agreement reached in 2026 pushes housekeeper pay above $100,000.
items.union: NY Hotel & Gaming Trades Council (AFL-CIO; UNITE HERE Local 6)
items.caveats: Boutique hotels and outer-borough limited-service hotels are often not union, so check each property on fairhotel.org.

items.name: Union hotel brands (Union Plus list)
items.what: Brands with many UNITE HERE-represented properties include Hilton, Marriott, Sheraton, Westin, Ritz-Carlton, Hyatt, Radisson, Holiday Inn, Best Western, and Comfort Inn, according to a Union Plus list.
items.caveats: The brand itself isn't what's union, only specific properties are. Always check fairhotel.org before booking.

items.name: UnionEats.org (Las Vegas union restaurants)
items.what: UnionEats.org is the Culinary Union's directory of more than 360 union restaurants on the Las Vegas Strip and downtown, including places like the MGM Grand Buffet and L'Atelier de Joel Robuchon.
items.caveats: This only covers Las Vegas.

items.name: Twin Cities union restaurants, bars & breweries (UNITE HERE Local 17)
items.what: UNITE HERE Local 17 covers Mancini's Char House in St. Paul, Jax Cafe in Minneapolis, FIKA Cafe at the American Swedish Institute, Fair State Brewing Cooperative, Indeed Brewing, Brother Justus Whiskey Co., The Minneapolis Club, First Avenue's production staff, Kelber Catering at the Minneapolis Convention Center, and the St. Paul RiverCentre.
items.caveats: This comes from Local 17's current contracts list. Verify before assuming a specific location is covered.

brand: twin cities union restaurants, bars & breweries

items.name: Chicago Federation of Labor union restaurant & vendor guide
items.what: The Chicago Federation of Labor keeps directories of union restaurants, barbecue spots, hotels, auto dealerships, moving companies, printers, photographers, and window washers around Chicago, linking to UNITE HERE Local 1 and UAW guides.
items.union: Chicago Federation of Labor (AFL-CIO) / UNITE HERE Local 1
items.caveats: This is a directory covering many businesses, not one place, and listings change over time.

brand: chicago federation of labor union restaurant & vendor guide

items.name: Twin Cities stadium & arena concessions
items.what: Food, beverage, and retail workers at Target Field (Twins), Target Center (Timberwolves and Lynx), US Bank Stadium (Vikings, run by Aramark, Fanatics, and Rank and Rally), Xcel Energy Center (Wild), Allianz Field (MN United), and Hennepin Theatre Trust venues all belong to UNITE HERE Local 17.
items.caveats: The company running concessions, like Delaware North, Aramark, or Levy, can change, and buying a ticket itself isn't a union purchase. Stagehands at most Twin Cities theaters belong to IATSE (International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees) Local 13.

items.name: Chicago stadium & arena concessions
items.what: Levy Restaurants concession workers at Wrigley Field (Cubs) and the United Center (Bulls and Blackhawks) belong to UNITE HERE Local 1. Levy also started running food service at Soldier Field in 2024.
items.caveats: This covers concession and food workers, not tickets or team staff.

items.name: MSP Airport food & lounge concessions
items.what: Workers for HMSHost, SSP, OTG, Areas, THS, Delta Sky Club, and LSG Sky Chefs at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport belong to UNITE HERE Local 17.
items.caveats: This is specific to MSP. Concessions at other airports vary, though many HMSHost airports elsewhere are also UNITE HERE.

items.name: Starbucks (Workers United stores)
items.what: More than 500 US Starbucks stores, with over 11,000 baristas, have voted to join Starbucks Workers United, an SEIU (Service Employees International Union) affiliate, since 2021, with multiple union stores in both Minnesota and Chicago.
items.caveats: There is still no first contract as of September 2026. The union has run 'No Contract, No Coffee' strikes since November 2025 and called for a boycott in August 2026, asking supporters not to buy at Starbucks until a contract is signed. Most of the company's roughly 9,000-plus stores remain non-union.

items.name: Cub Foods (UNFI corporate & franchise stores, Twin Cities)
items.what: Nearly 3,000 workers at UNFI-owned Cub stores and Haug's Cub Foods in the Twin Cities ratified a three-year UFCW Local 663 contract in July 2025. Jerry's Cub and Radermacher's Cub franchise stores are also under Local 663 contracts.
items.caveats: Cub is Minnesota's largest union grocer. Some outstate stores may fall under other UFCW locals, like Local 1189 in St. Paul and the east metro.

items.name: Lunds & Byerlys
items.what: Lunds and Byerlys, the upscale Twin Cities grocer, has store workers represented by UFCW Local 663. The union won this contract after threatening a strike around the 2023 holidays, and it was renegotiated in 2025.

items.name: Kowalski's Markets
items.what: Kowalski's Markets, a family-owned Twin Cities grocer, has workers under UFCW Local 663 contracts.

items.name: Knowlan's Festival Foods, Jerry's Foods & other Twin Cities independents
items.what: UFCW Local 663 contracts cover Knowlan's Festival Foods, Jerry's Foods, Oxendale's Market, Almsted's Fresh Market, Driskill's Downtown Market, Mound Jubilee, King's County Market in Andover, Everett's Foods, Cooper's Foods, and Ingebretsen's Scandinavian Gifts.
items.caveats: Knowlan's Festival Foods in Minnesota is a completely different, unrelated chain from the non-union Skogen's Festival Foods in Wisconsin, so don't mix them up.

brand: knowlan's festival foods, jerry's foods & other twin cities independents

items.name: Jewel-Osco (Albertsons) - Chicagoland
items.what: Jewel Food Stores and Osco Drug workers across the Chicago area are represented by UFCW Local 881, the region's largest union grocer.

items.name: Mariano's (Kroger) - Chicagoland
items.what: Mariano's Fresh Market stores, a Kroger banner, are represented by UFCW Local 881 in the Chicago area.

items.name: Kroger family of stores (union banners)
items.what: UFCW represents workers at roughly two-thirds of Kroger stores, including the Kroger, Fred Meyer, King Soopers, City Market, Ralphs, Food 4 Less, Fry's, Smith's, QFC, Dillons, Baker's, Gerbes, Pick 'n Save and Metro Market (Wisconsin, UFCW 1473), Mariano's, Jay C, Pay Less, Owen's, Ruler Foods, and Harris Teeter banners, though Harris Teeter is only partly covered.
items.caveats: About a third of Kroger stores are not union, mostly in the South, including many Kroger and Harris Teeter locations there. Check with the local UFCW to be sure.

items.name: Albertsons / Safeway family (union banners)
items.what: A majority of Albertsons Companies workers are UFCW-represented, across the Safeway, Albertsons, Vons, Pavilions, Jewel-Osco, Shaw's, Star Market, Acme, Carrs, Haggen, and Kings/Balducci's banners.
items.caveats: The Texas banners, Tom Thumb, Randalls, and United Supermarkets, along with some others, are largely not union.

items.name: Stop & Shop and Giant (Ahold Delhaize)
items.what: Stop & Shop stores in New England, New York and New Jersey and Giant Food stores in DC, Maryland, Virginia and Delaware are staffed by workers who belong to UFCW (United Food and Commercial Workers).
items.caveats: The Giant Company in Pennsylvania is a different Ahold Delhaize banner and is mostly non-union, and so are Food Lion and Hannaford.

items.name: Meijer (Michigan)
items.what: More than 25,000 Meijer workers in Michigan are covered by four-year contracts with UFCW Local 951 that took effect in February 2024.
items.caveats: This only covers Michigan stores. Meijer locations in Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Kentucky and Wisconsin are generally not union.

items.name: Schnucks (St. Louis / Illinois)
items.what: Schnucks stores in Illinois and the St. Louis area have UFCW contracts, Local 881 in Illinois and Local 655 in Missouri.

items.name: Costco (Teamsters warehouses)
items.what: About 18,000 Costco workers at roughly 56 warehouses, mostly in California, New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Virginia and Washington, plus fleet drivers, are Teamsters. The national master agreement was ratified in March 2025 after the union threatened to strike, and fleet drivers ratified their own agreement in April 2025.
items.caveats: Union warehouses are still a small share of the total, around 56 out of more than 600. Midwest Costcos, including Minnesota and Illinois, are not union, and non-union locations generally pay close to union wages anyway.

items.name: CVS Pharmacy (Chicagoland stores)
items.what: CVS workers in the Chicago area belong to UFCW Local 881. UFCW also represents CVS, Walgreens and Rite Aid workers in parts of California, New York and Pennsylvania.
items.caveats: This coverage is regional. Most CVS stores nationwide are not union.

items.name: Chicagoland new-car dealership service departments (IAM Local 701)
items.what: Technicians at roughly 155 new-car dealerships in the Chicago area belong to IAM (International Association of Machinists) Automobile Mechanics Local 701. A four-year contract was ratified in September 2021 after an eight-week strike and was renegotiated in 2025.
items.caveats: This covers service technicians, not sales staff. Check Local 701's shop list or ask the service manager, since most dealerships in the US are not union.

items.name: Twin Cities union dealership & truck shops (Teamsters Local 974 / IAM District 77)
items.what: Teamsters Local 974 in Minneapolis and IAM District 77 represent mechanics at a number of auto and truck dealerships and repair shops in the Twin Cities. Local 974 publishes a shop locations list.
items.caveats: Specific dealership names aren't listed here, so check Local 974's shop list or IAM77.org. Most Minnesota dealerships are not union.

brand: twin cities union dealership & truck shops

items.name: American Airlines
items.what: American is the most heavily unionized major US airline. Pilots belong to APA, flight attendants to APFA, mechanics and fleet service to a joint TWU-IAM association, and passenger service agents to CWA-IBEW.

items.name: United Airlines
items.what: United's pilots belong to ALPA, its roughly 28,000 flight attendants to AFA-CWA, its mechanics to the Teamsters (IBT), and ramp and customer service workers to IAM.
items.caveats: Flight attendants rejected a tentative contract in July 2025 and were in mediation, so check with AFA for the current status.

items.name: Southwest Airlines
items.what: Southwest is about 83 percent unionized across twelve unions. Pilots belong to SWAPA, flight attendants to TWU Local 556, ramp workers to TWU 555, mechanics to AMFA, and customer service to IAM.

items.name: Alaska Airlines (incl. Hawaiian)
items.what: Alaska mainline is about 84 percent unionized, with ALPA pilots, AFA-CWA flight attendants and IAM ground crews. Hawaiian Airlines is about 81 percent union.
items.caveats: Horizon Air, Alaska's regional subsidiary, is only about 42 percent unionized.

items.name: Frontier, Spirit & JetBlue (partial)
items.what: Frontier and Spirit pilots belong to ALPA and their flight attendants to AFA-CWA. JetBlue pilots belong to ALPA and flight attendants to TWU, putting JetBlue at about 51 percent union overall.
items.caveats: JetBlue's ground crews and mechanics are largely non-union.

items.name: Sun Country Airlines (Minneapolis)
items.what: Sun Country, based at Minneapolis-St. Paul, has pilots represented by ALPA and flight attendants represented by Teamsters Local 2000.
items.caveats: This is based on general knowledge of Sun Country's union setup rather than a confirmed union-made list.

items.name: Hertz (Teamsters airport locations)
items.what: Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty workers at many major airports are Teamsters, covered by a Western Regional Agreement from 2024 and local contracts at airports including SFO, LAX, DFW, PBI and SLC.
items.caveats: Coverage varies location by location, and the Teamsters struck Hertz at some airports in early 2025. Neighborhood rental locations away from airports are mostly non-union.

items.name: Avis Budget (Teamsters airport locations)
items.what: Avis and Budget rental agents and shuttle drivers at several airports, including Orlando and the Bay Area airports, are Teamsters.
items.caveats: This is location by location only, so check before assuming a given branch is union.

items.name: Union movers (Teamsters) - how to find
items.what: Several Teamsters locals publish lists of union moving companies. Local 814 has a Find a Mover tool for New York City, Local 120 has a Union Vendors page for Minnesota, Iowa and the Dakotas, and the Chicago Federation of Labor keeps its own moving company list. Many United, Mayflower, Allied and North American agents in those markets are Teamsters shops.
items.caveats: The van line brand alone doesn't guarantee a union crew. The local agent has to be a Teamsters shop, so ask to see the contract.

items.name: UPS
items.what: More than 340,000 UPS drivers, package handlers and feeder drivers are Teamsters under the 2023 to 2028 National Master Agreement, the largest private-sector union contract in North America.
items.caveats: UPS pilots belong to their own independent union, IPA, not the Teamsters. The Teamsters sued UPS in 2026 over driver buyouts, and the current contract runs through July 2028.

items.name: USPS (US Postal Service)
items.what: Essentially the entire US Postal Service workforce is unionized. Letter carriers belong to NALC, clerks to APWU, rural carriers to NRLCA, and mail handlers to NPMHU.

items.name: Amalgamated Bank
items.what: Amalgamated Bank is the largest union-owned bank in the country, majority owned by Workers United, an SEIU affiliate, and its own employees are unionized. It offers nationwide online and mobile banking along with branches in New York City, Washington DC and San Francisco.
items.caveats: There are no Midwest branches, but customers get access to 40,000 surcharge-free ATMs.

items.name: AFL-CIO Employees Federal Credit Union
items.what: This is a credit union based in Washington DC, set up for staff and members of the AFL-CIO and its affiliated unions.
items.caveats: Membership is limited to people who work for or belong to AFL-CIO affiliated organizations. Many local labor councils sponsor their own credit unions too, so ask your local.

items.name: Union Plus (AFL-CIO member benefits)
items.what: Union Plus is the AFL-CIO's member benefits program. It includes a Union Plus credit card, mortgage program, an AT&T wireless discount, insurance, a travel center, and entertainment discounts, and it also publishes union-made shopping guides.
items.caveats: You need to be a union member to use it.

items.name: Ullico (Union Labor Life Insurance Co.)
items.what: Ullico is a union-owned insurance and investment company founded in 1927 by the AFL. It offers life insurance, health coverage, and the Ullico Select marketplace for individual union members and their families.
items.union: Owned by unions and union pension funds (AFL-CIO affiliated)
items.caveats: Most of its products are sold through unions and benefit funds rather than directly to retail customers.

items.name: AT&T (wireless & wireline)
items.what: AT&T is the largest unionized telecom employer in the country, with more than 55,000 CWA and IBEW members. Wireline service is union across the Midwest, Southwest, Southeast and West, and AT&T Mobility retail and call center workers in 36 states are covered under the Mobility "Orange" contract, covering about 9,000 workers.
items.caveats: Some Mobility regions and authorized retailers, like Prime Communications, are not union, though corporate stores in the Midwest are typically CWA.

items.name: Verizon (wireline; some wireless retail)
items.what: Verizon's wireline Fios technicians and call centers in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic are CWA and IBEW, with contracts ratified in April 2026. A handful of Verizon Wireless retail stores are also CWA, including one in Brooklyn since 2014 and two in Everett and Lynnwood, Washington since 2022.
items.caveats: Verizon Wireless retail overall and Verizon's Midwest operations are overwhelmingly non-union, and Verizon has faced accusations of resisting wireless organizing.

items.name: Minnesota Star Tribune & St. Paul Pioneer Press
items.what: Newsroom staff at the Star Tribune, whose contract was ratified in 2024, the Pioneer Press, the Duluth News Tribune, MinnPost, the Duluth Labor World, the Minneapolis Labor Review and the St. Paul Union Advocate all belong to the Minnesota Newspaper and Communications Guild, part of NewsGuild-CWA.
items.caveats: Printing and distribution staff are covered separately and vary by outlet.

brand: minnesota star tribune & st. paul pioneer press

items.name: Chicago Tribune & Chicago Sun-Times
items.what: Newsroom staff at the Chicago Tribune belong to the Chicago Tribune Guild, part of NewsGuild-CWA, with a contract from 2023, and the Chicago Sun-Times newsroom has its own Guild.
items.caveats: The Tribune is owned by Alden Global Capital, and the Guild has been openly critical of that ownership.

items.name: NewsGuild-CWA newsrooms (national)
items.what: NewsGuild-CWA represents journalists at more than 300 outlets, including the New York Times, Washington Post, LA Times, Wall Street Journal (through IAPE), the Associated Press, Reuters, the Chicago Tribune, the Star Tribune, the Denver Post, the Philadelphia Inquirer, Buzzfeed and Vox. Subscribing to these outlets supports union newsrooms.
items.caveats: The union covers editorial staff, not necessarily the ownership or distribution side of these outlets.

items.name: Allied Printing Trades label (union 'bug')
items.what: The Allied Printing Trades Council "bug" is a mark certifying that printed work was done in a union shop under CWA printing contracts or IAM and GCC contracts. AlliedLabel.org has a Find a Union Shop directory, and the Chicago Federation of Labor and various state labor federations keep their own lists of union printers. Most union and political mailings carry this label.
items.union: International Allied Printing Trades Council (CWA, IAM)
items.caveats: Look for the bug along with a local council number printed on the piece.

items.name: Labor 411 (union directory)
items.subcategory: How to find union goods & services
items.what: Labor 411 is a searchable national directory of union-made products and union services, covering restaurants, hotels, grocers, printers and auto shops, with regional guides. It's run by the Los Angeles County Federation of Labor.
items.caveats: Listings can go stale, so it's worth double checking before relying on them.

items.name: Union Label & Service Trades Dept. (unionlabel.org)
items.subcategory: How to find union goods & services
items.what: This AFL-CIO department runs unionlabel.org, which publishes a Do Buy list covering union airlines, hotels and products, along with a Don't Buy boycott list.

items.name: Union cinemas & live entertainment (IATSE/AFM)
items.what: Broadway and most touring Broadway shows use IATSE stagehands, AFM musicians and Actors' Equity performers. The Minnesota Orchestra and Chicago Symphony are AFM. Hennepin Theatre Trust venues in Minneapolis use IATSE Local 13 for stagehands and UNITE HERE Local 17 for front-of-house staff, and major league sports venues generally use IATSE and UNITE HERE crews.
items.union: IATSE, AFM, Actors' Equity, UNITE HERE
items.caveats: Ticket resellers like Ticketmaster and StubHub are not union. The union labor is in the production and the venue staff, not the ticketing.

items.name: Union-made professional sports (players' unions)
items.what: Players in MLB, the NFL, the NBA, the NHL, the WNBA and MLS are all unionized through their respective players associations, and umpires and referees have their own unions too. Watching a game at a venue with union concessions, like Target Field or Wrigley Field, supports union labor twice over.
items.union: MLBPA, NFLPA, NBPA, NHLPA, WNBPA, MLSPA
items.caveats: Minor league and college athletes are largely not unionized.

items.name: Whole Foods Philadelphia (Spring Garden store)
items.what: The Whole Foods store on Spring Garden Street in Philadelphia was the first Whole Foods to unionize. Workers voted to join UFCW Local 1776 in January 2025, and the NLRB (National Labor Relations Board) upheld the election in June 2026.
items.caveats: This is a single store with no contract yet, and Whole Foods is contesting the result. All of the other roughly 530 Whole Foods stores are non-union.

items.name: Trader Joe's United stores
items.what: Five Trader Joe's stores have unionized: Hadley, Massachusetts in 2022, the Lyndale Avenue store in Minneapolis in 2022, Louisville, Kentucky in 2023, Oakland, California in 2023, and the North Center store in Chicago, certified in July 2026.
items.caveats: None of these stores has a first contract yet as of 2026, and the company has fought the union at each step. The roughly 570 other Trader Joe's stores are non-union.

items.name: Teamsters Local 120 union vendor list (MN/IA/ND/SD)
items.what: Teamsters Local 120, based in Blaine, Minnesota, posts a Union Vendors page listing Teamster-signatory movers, dealerships, beverage distributors and other services across Minnesota, Iowa and the Dakotas.
items.caveats: Treat it as a lookup tool to check specific businesses rather than a list to browse from memory.

items.name: Peerless Chain Company (Kito Crosby) - Winona, Minnesota
items.subcategory: Chain, chain slings, tie-downs, tire chains
items.what: Peerless Chain's plant in Winona, Minnesota makes welded and weldless chain, including Grade 70, 80 and 100 transport and lifting chain, chain slings, binder and tie-down chain, tire chains and related hardware. It's made by around 130 or more IAM Local 1030 members. The company is now part of Kito Crosby.
items.caveats: The four-year IAM contract was ratified in September 2021 and expired in September 2025, so check whether it's been renewed. Kito Crosby's other US plants, including Crosby in Tulsa and Longview and Kito Harrington, are not known to be union. Peerless also imports some chain and accessories, so check the tag for where it was made.

items.name: 3M - Springfield, Missouri plant (USW, organized Dec 2025)
items.what: About 380 workers at 3M's Springfield, Missouri plant, which makes adhesives, sealants and specialty products for the automotive and aerospace industries, voted to join the United Steelworkers (USW) in December 2025. It's the only 3M US manufacturing site with a recent union win. 3M's fall-protection plant in Red Wing, Minnesota, which makes DBI-SALA gear, and its respirator plant in Aberdeen, South Dakota, have no known union.
items.caveats: This plant is newly organized and doesn't have a contract yet. It doesn't mean 3M hard hats, respirators, harnesses or Scotch and Post-it consumer products are union-made.

items.name: Milwaukee Tool
items.what: Milwaukee Tool has US plants in Wisconsin and Mississippi that handle hand tools, accessories and some assembly, though most of the product line is made in China and Vietnam.
items.caveats: Employees have reported that neither the Wisconsin nor the Mississippi plants are unionized. The company is owned by TTI, based in Hong Kong. It's often assumed to be union because of its heavy marketing to tradespeople.

items.name: Southwire
items.what: Southwire makes Romex and NM-B and THHN building wire, SIMpull cable, and Southwire-branded electrician tools, with plants in Carrollton, Georgia and elsewhere in the US.
items.caveats: Southwire is the largest US building-wire maker. It's privately held and has long been non-union, and its hand tools are mostly imported.

items.name: Encore Wire (now Prysmian, McKinney TX)
items.what: Encore Wire, now owned by Prysmian, makes copper building wire including NM-B, THHN and URD cable at a single campus in McKinney, Texas.
items.caveats: Encore's SEC filings state its employees are not represented by a union. Prysmian acquired the company in 2024. Unlike Prysmian's Marshall, Texas plant, which is UAW, the McKinney plant remains non-union as far as is known.

items.name: Lincoln Electric
items.what: Lincoln Electric makes welding machines and consumables in Cleveland and Euclid, Ohio.
items.caveats: The company is known for its guaranteed employment policy and incentive pay system, and its elected employee Advisory Board is credited with keeping the plant non-union for more than a hundred years. It's made in the USA, but it's not union.

items.name: Werner Ladder
items.what: Werner ladders, both fiberglass and aluminum, are mostly made now in Juarez, Mexico. The company is headquartered in Greenville, Pennsylvania, and its former union plants in Greenville and in Louisville, Kentucky have both closed, with the work shipped to Mexico.
items.caveats: Werner was historically union in Greenville, so buyers still assume that's true today. A 2010 filing at a Merced, California plant with 75 employees shows a union existed there once, but its current status is unknown. Most Werner ladders sold today are made in Mexico.

items.name: Craftsman
items.what: Craftsman hand tools are now made by Stanley Black & Decker.
items.caveats: Labor 411 still lists Craftsman as IBEW and Teamsters-made from the old Sears era, when many items came from union US contractors. Stanley Black & Decker's Fort Worth, Texas Craftsman plant closed in 2023, and most Craftsman tools are now imported, so don't assume they're union-made.

items.name: Round House (Shawnee, OK)
items.what: Round House makes bib overalls, jeans, jackets and aprons in Shawnee, Oklahoma, turning out about 1,000 pairs a day. It's often assumed to be union because it's sold through UnionLabel.com and gets confused with the separate Union Line brand.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but there's no union claim on the company's site, its FAQ, or retailer pages. UnionLabel.com lists it only as sewn in the USA, without a union designation, unlike Carhartt and Thorogood listed on the same page.

items.name: White's Boots (Spokane, WA)
items.what: White's Boots makes handmade logger and smokejumper boots in Spokane, Washington. The company is owned by LaCrosse Footwear and ABC-Mart, the same parent as Danner.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but doesn't appear on any union-made list, including Labor 411, UFCW or the Northwest Labor Press, unlike its sister brand Danner.

items.name: Nicks Handmade Boots (Spokane, WA)
items.what: Nicks Handmade Boots makes heritage work boots by hand in Spokane, Washington.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA, but no union affiliation shows up on any union-made source.

items.name: Dickies (VF/Williamson-Dickie)
items.what: Dickies workwear, made by VF and Williamson-Dickie, is produced overseas and in Mexico, with no US union plants.
items.caveats: It's commonly assumed to be union because of its workwear heritage, but it's imported and non-union.

items.name: Duluth Trading Co.
items.what: Duluth Trading workwear is mostly imported, with no union manufacturing involved.
items.caveats: The marketing evokes American workers, but the product itself is imported and non-union.

items.name: Carhartt, imported lines
items.what: This covers all Carhartt product that isn't labeled Made in USA or Union Made, which is the majority of the catalog, plus the Carhartt WIP line.
items.caveats: Carhartt stopped separating its domestic and imported inventory in 2009, so check the label for the words Union Made before buying.

items.name: Red Wing, Potosi, MO & Clarksville, AR plants; Irish Setter imports
items.what: Red Wing also makes boots at plants in Potosi, Missouri, opened in 1994, and Clarksville, Arkansas, opened in 2003, alongside imported Red Wing and Irish Setter styles.
items.union: None confirmed (UFCW 655 petition filed at Potosi April 2022; result unconfirmed)
items.caveats: Workers at the Potosi plant have cited a wage gap compared with the union Minnesota plant. Only styles made at the Red Wing, Minnesota plant are on the union list.

brand: red wing, potosi, mo & clarksville, ar plants; irish setter imports

items.name: Justin Boots / Tony Lama / Nocona (Justin Brands)
items.what: Justin Brands makes Justin, Tony Lama and Nocona boots, with some styles made in El Paso, Texas and many imported.
items.caveats: None of these appear on Labor 411, UFCW or Workers United union-made lists, and the union status of the El Paso plant couldn't be confirmed, so treat it as non-union unless you find documentation saying otherwise.

items.name: Nokona ballgloves (Nocona, TX)
items.what: Nokona makes the only baseball gloves still handmade in the USA, in Nocona, Texas.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA, but no union affiliation shows up in company or press coverage.

items.name: Pointer Brand (L.C. King Mfg., Bristol, TN)
items.what: Pointer Brand, made by L.C. King Manufacturing, has produced hickory-stripe overalls and chore coats in Bristol, Tennessee since 1913.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but doesn't appear on any union-made list.

items.name: Big Bill (Codet Inc.)
items.what: Big Bill, made by Codet Inc., produces flame-resistant and general workwear in Cowansville, Quebec and at a US facility, and is sold through UnionLabel.com.
items.caveats: The company itself makes no union claim, and UnionLabel.com lists it only as Made in USA and Canada, without a union designation.

items.name: North Star Glove Co. (Tacoma, WA)
items.what: North Star Glove Co. has made leather work gloves in Tacoma, Washington since 1910, and is sold through UnionLabel.com.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA, but no union claim appears on the company's site or on union-made lists.

items.name: Midwest Glove & Gear (Chillicothe, MO)
items.what: Midwest Glove & Gear makes leather and other work gloves in Chillicothe, Missouri.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but doesn't appear on union-made lists.

items.name: Darn Tough / Fox River / Thorlo socks
items.what: These are US-made socks, from Northfield, Vermont, Osage, Iowa and Statesville, North Carolina, and people often assume they're union like Wigwam.
items.caveats: Only Wigwam, made in Sheboygan by UFCW workers, actually appears on union-made lists.

items.name: New Balance (USA-made 990 series)
items.what: New Balance's Made in USA 990 series sneakers are made in Skowhegan and Norridgewock, Maine and in Lawrence, Massachusetts, and are sold through UnionLabel.com.
items.caveats: They're assembled in the US but not union, and UnionLabel.com lists them without a union designation.

items.name: Filson (Seattle) / Wesco (Scappoose, OR) / KEEN Utility (Portland)
items.what: Filson in Seattle, Wesco in Scappoose, Oregon and KEEN Utility in Portland are all Pacific Northwest heritage workwear and boot makers with US factories.
items.caveats: None of them appear on the Northwest Labor Press, Labor 411 or UFCW union-made lists, which instead name Danner as the region's union bootmaker.

items.name: Texas Jeans USA / Origin USA / Raleigh Denim / Tellason / Railcar
items.what: Texas Jeans USA, Origin USA, Raleigh Denim, Tellason and Railcar are US-made denim brands often marketed to union members.
items.caveats: Promote Unions' own list of jeans for union members notes that none of these brands actually state a union affiliation.

items.name: Sumitomo / Dunlop tires - Buffalo (Tonawanda), NY plant
items.what: This plant in Tonawanda, near Buffalo, New York made Dunlop motorcycle tires and some Sumitomo and Falken passenger tires, marked with DOT code DA.
items.caveats: The plant is closed. Sumitomo Rubber USA announced its immediate closure on November 7, 2024, affecting about 1,500 USW Local 135L jobs, with final shutdown on May 15, 2025. Any Dunlop motorcycle tires or Falken and Sumitomo passenger tires carrying DOT code DA are old stock, since current Dunlop motorcycle tires are now imported. Treat this as a plant to watch rather than a current source of union-made tires.

items.name: Tesla (Model 3/Y/S/X, Cybertruck) - Fremont CA, Austin TX
items.what: All Tesla US assembly, covering the Model 3, Y, S and X and the Cybertruck, built in Fremont, California and Austin, Texas, is non-union. The UAW has an organizing campaign underway but no election has been held.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but not union, and it doesn't appear on any UAW guide.

items.name: Rivian (R1T, R1S, EDV) - Normal, IL
items.what: Rivian's R1T, R1S and EDV, built in Normal, Illinois, are non-union. The UAW has an active organizing drive there but no contract.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but not union.

items.name: Lucid (Air, Gravity) - Casa Grande, AZ
items.what: Lucid's Air and Gravity models, assembled in Casa Grande, Arizona, are non-union.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but not union.

items.name: Mercedes-Benz (GLE, GLS, EQS SUV) - Vance, AL
items.what: Mercedes-Benz builds the GLE, GLS and EQS SUV in Vance, Alabama. Workers there voted 56 percent against joining the UAW in May 2024.
items.caveats: It's made in the USA but not union.

items.name: Toyota US plants (Georgetown KY, Princeton IN, San Antonio TX, Huntsville AL, Blue Springs MS) and Cambridge/Woodstock, ON
items.what: Toyota builds the Camry, RAV4, Highlander, Grand Highlander, Sienna, Sequoia and Tundra, along with the Corolla in Mississippi and the Corolla Cross and Mazda CX-50 in Huntsville, Alabama, at plants in Georgetown, Kentucky, Princeton, Indiana, San Antonio, Texas, Huntsville, Alabama and Blue Springs, Mississippi. Its Canadian plants in Cambridge and Woodstock, Ontario are also non-union.
items.caveats: These vehicles are heavily marketed as American-made, but none of the plants are union. A UAW organizing effort is ongoing at Georgetown.

items.name: Honda / Acura US plants (Marysville & East Liberty OH, Lincoln AL, Greensburg IN) and Alliston, ON
items.what: Honda and Acura build the Accord, Civic (in Indiana and Ontario), CR-V, Pilot, Passport, Odyssey, Ridgeline, and the Acura TLX, MDX, RDX and Integra at non-union plants in Marysville and East Liberty, Ohio, Lincoln, Alabama, Greensburg, Indiana, and Alliston, Ontario.
items.caveats: These are made in the USA or Canada but not union.

items.name: Nissan (Smyrna TN, Canton MS), Hyundai (Montgomery AL), Kia (West Point GA), Subaru (Lafayette IN), BMW (Spartanburg SC), Mazda-Toyota (Huntsville AL), Volvo (Ridgeville SC)
items.what: Nissan builds the Rogue, Pathfinder, Frontier and Titan in Smyrna, Tennessee and Canton, Mississippi. Hyundai builds the Santa Fe and Tucson in Montgomery, Alabama, and the Ioniq 5 in Savannah, Georgia. Kia builds the Telluride and Sorento in West Point, Georgia. Subaru builds the Outback, Ascent and Crosstrek in Lafayette, Indiana. BMW builds the X3, X5 and X7 in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Mazda and Toyota jointly build vehicles in Huntsville, Alabama, and Volvo builds the EX90 in Ridgeville, South Carolina. All of this US assembly is non-union.
items.caveats: These are made in the USA, but none of it is union. Nissan's Canton, Mississippi plant voted against the UAW in 2017.

items.name: Detroit Three models built in Mexico (Ram HD 2500/3500, Ram ProMaster, Ford Maverick, Bronco Sport, Mustang Mach-E, Chevy Equinox/Blazer/Equinox EV/Blazer EV, Cadillac Optiq, Jeep Compass, GMC Terrain)
items.what: Several vehicles carry American badges but are actually assembled in Mexico, including the Ram HD 2500 and 3500, Ram ProMaster, Ford Maverick, Bronco Sport, Mustang Mach-E, Chevy Equinox, Blazer, Equinox EV and Blazer EV, Cadillac Optiq, Jeep Compass and GMC Terrain, built at plants in Saltillo, Hermosillo, Cuautitlan, Ramos Arizpe, San Luis Potosi and Toluca. None of these are UAW-built.
items.caveats: None of these appear on the 2026 UAW guide. The Jeep Compass is slated to move production to Brampton, Ontario, a Unifor plant, so this may be worth rechecking in 2027.

brand: detroit three models built in mexico

items.name: Non-union US tire plants: Goodyear Lawton OK & Tupelo MS; Bridgestone Aiken SC & Wilson NC; Michelin SC/AL/OK plants; Continental Mt. Vernon IL / Sumter SC / Clinton MS; Hankook Clarksville TN; Toyo White GA; Nokian Dayton TN; Giti Richburg SC; Pirelli Rome GA
items.what: Several Made in USA tires come from plants that are not on the USW/AFL-CIO union tire list, including Goodyear's Lawton, Oklahoma and Tupelo, Mississippi plants, Bridgestone's Aiken, South Carolina and Wilson, North Carolina plants, Michelin's plants in South Carolina, Alabama and Oklahoma, Continental's plants in Mount Vernon, Illinois, Sumter, South Carolina and Clinton, Mississippi, Hankook in Clarksville, Tennessee, Toyo in White, Georgia, Nokian in Dayton, Tennessee, Giti in Richburg, South Carolina, and Pirelli in Rome, Georgia.
items.caveats: The same brand name, like Goodyear, Bridgestone, Michelin or Firestone, can be union or non-union depending on the plant, so check the DOT code on the tire against the AFL-CIO union tire list.

brand: non-union us  plants: goodyear lawton ok & tupelo ms; bridgestone aiken sc & wilson nc; michelin sc

items.name: Polaris (RZR, Ranger, Indian Motorcycle - Spirit Lake IA, Huntsville AL, Roseau MN)
items.what: Polaris builds its RZR and Ranger off-road vehicles and Indian Motorcycle builds its bikes in the USA, with Indian assembled in Spirit Lake, Iowa and other plants in Huntsville, Alabama and Roseau, Minnesota, but none of it is union.
items.caveats: Indian Motorcycle is commonly confused with the union-made Harley-Davidson, but neither Polaris nor Indian appears on any union-made list.

items.name: Yuengling
items.what: Yuengling brews beer in Pottsville, Pennsylvania, Tampa, Florida, and at a Fort Worth, Texas joint venture with Molson Coors.
items.caveats: Pottsville workers voted out Teamsters Local 830 in 2006 after the owner lobbied for right-to-work laws, and the Teamsters called a boycott afterward. The Fort Worth joint venture cans are made at a union Molson Coors plant, so only that production is union-made.

items.name: Bell's Brewery (Kirin/Lion)
items.what: Bell's Brewery, owned by Kirin and Lion, brews in Comstock, Michigan.
items.caveats: It doesn't appear on any union-made list. Kirin's union operations are in Japan, not here. New Belgium, under the same ownership, used to be an employee stock ownership company but is now non-union too.

items.name: Sierra Nevada
items.what: Sierra Nevada brews in Chico, California and Mills River, North Carolina.
items.caveats: It's family owned with a reputation for treating employees well, but there's no union contract, and it's absent from the AFL-CIO, Teamsters and Labor 411 lists.

items.name: Sam Adams, Breinigsville PA brewery
items.what: Boston Beer runs a brewery in Breinigsville, Pennsylvania.
items.caveats: The union status of the Pennsylvania brewery hasn't been confirmed. Only the Cincinnati brewery is confirmed Teamsters, so don't assume all Sam Adams is union-made.

items.name: Anchor Brewing
items.what: Anchor Brewing, based in San Francisco, was the first unionized craft brewery in the US, joining the ILWU (International Longshore and Warehouse Union) in 2019.
items.caveats: Sapporo closed the brewery in July 2023. It was bought by Hamdi Ulukaya, the founder of Chobani, in 2024, but as of 2025 it hadn't reopened and there's no contract.

items.name: Goose Island Chicago (Fulton St.) brewery / Great Lakes / Surly
items.what: Goose Island's Fulton Street brewpub in Chicago, along with Great Lakes and Surly, are craft brewpubs.
items.caveats: Union organizing drives at these brewpubs have failed. Note that Goose Island's packaged beer, brewed at Anheuser-Busch's union plants, is union-made, and Labor 411 credits it to the Teamsters (IBT).

items.name: Coors, Golden CO and Shenandoah VA breweries
items.what: Molson Coors' two largest US breweries are in Golden, Colorado and Shenandoah, Virginia.
items.caveats: The Golden plant has only a handful of IUOE Local 9 members, and the Shenandoah plant is non-union, so Coors from these plants isn't really union-made even though Coors sometimes shows up on union lists.

brand: coors, golden  and shenandoah va breweries

items.name: Hostess (Twinkies, Ding Dongs, Ho Hos, J.M. Smucker)
items.what: Hostess makes Twinkies, Ding Dongs and Ho Hos at plants in Emporia, Kansas, Columbus, Georgia and Indianapolis, Indiana. The brand is now owned by J.M. Smucker.
items.caveats: Before its 2012 liquidation, Hostess was union with BCTGM (Bakery, Confectionery, Tobacco Workers and Grain Millers) and Teamsters members. After Apollo and Metropoulos reopened the plants, they did so without union workers. Smucker bought Hostess in 2023.

items.name: Chobani
items.what: Chobani makes yogurt in Twin Falls, Idaho and South Edmeston, New York.
items.caveats: The company offers employee equity and strong benefits, but it isn't union and doesn't appear on any union-made list.

items.name: Nature's Own / Wonder / Dave's Killer Bread (Flowers Foods)
items.what: Nature's Own, Wonder and Dave's Killer Bread are made at Flowers Foods bakeries, mostly in the Southeast.
items.caveats: Flowers Foods is largely non-union and relies on independent distributors. Only Tastykake, made in Philadelphia by BCTGM workers, and a small number of other Flowers bakeries are union.

items.name: Brach's (Ferrara)
items.what: Brach's candy corn and similar candies are now made in Mexico.
items.caveats: The original union Chicago Brach's plant closed in 2004, and production moved to Linares, Mexico.

items.name: Oreo / Chips Ahoy! from Salinas, Mexico
items.what: Mondelez's plant in Salinas, Mexico supplies part of the US supply of Oreo, Chips Ahoy and belVita.
items.caveats: Check the package. Units marked Made in Mexico don't come from the union BCTGM bakeries. Oreos made in Chicago, Portland or Richmond are union-made.

items.name: Snyder's of Hanover / Pepperidge Farm / Cape Cod (Campbell Snacks)
items.what: Snyder's of Hanover, Pepperidge Farm and Cape Cod chips, all under Campbell Snacks, are made in Hanover, Pennsylvania and other plants.
items.caveats: Don't confuse this with Snyder of Berlin, which is UFCW and Teamsters. Campbell's soup plants are UFCW, but the Campbell Snacks brands themselves don't appear on union lists.

items.name: Frito-Lay non-union plants
items.what: Most Frito-Lay plants in the US are non-union.
items.caveats: The same Lay's or Doritos label can come from a union plant, like Topeka or Vancouver, Washington, or a non-union one. The plant code printed on the bag is the only way to tell which.

items.name: Starbucks packaged coffee
items.what: Starbucks roasts packaged coffee at plants in Kent, Washington, York, Pennsylvania and Augusta, Georgia.
items.caveats: These roasting plants are non-union. Starbucks Workers United represents cafe baristas, not the packaged coffee side. Teavana tea bottled at the Adirondack plant is Teamsters, though.

items.name: Jack Daniel's (Brown-Forman)
items.what: Jack Daniel's, made by Brown-Forman, is distilled in Lynchburg, Tennessee.
items.caveats: It's often assumed to be union because Brown-Forman's Louisville plant is UFCW 10D, but the Lynchburg distillery isn't confirmed on any UFCW list.

items.name: Nucor steel (rebar, beams, decking, joists)
items.what: Nucor is the largest steelmaker in the US, and all of its rebar, beams, decking and joists are made domestically at electric-arc mini-mills.
items.caveats: None of Nucor's mills are unionized, and the company's culture is openly opposed to unions. It's often assumed to be union simply because it's American-made steel.

items.name: Steel Dynamics (SDI) steel
items.what: Steel Dynamics (SDI) makes flat-rolled and structural steel in the US at mini-mills in Indiana, Texas and Mississippi.
items.caveats: Like Nucor, it follows the non-union mini-mill model. This hasn't been confirmed by a union source directly, but there's no known USW representation there.

items.name: Southwire wire and cable (Romex NM-B)
items.what: Southwire makes building wire, including Romex NM-B, at its Carrollton, Georgia plant and other US locations. It's the most common Made in USA Romex found at big-box stores.
items.caveats: The company is family owned and has historically been non-union, though some plants it has acquired over time may have unions. People often assume it's union because electricians, who are IBEW, are the ones installing it.

items.name: Encore Wire (Prysmian) building wire
items.what: Encore Wire, now part of Prysmian, makes copper building wire entirely at its campus in McKinney, Texas.
items.caveats: This single campus is non-union. Prysmian acquired the company in 2024.

items.name: Lutron dimmers and lighting controls
items.what: Lutron designs and assembles dimmers, switches and shades in Coopersburg, Pennsylvania and other US plants.
items.caveats: The company is privately held and non-union, and it has been shifting more production offshore to Mexico and China. It doesn't appear on any union-made list.

items.name: Leviton wiring devices
items.what: Leviton makes outlets, switches and dimmers, with some assembly done in the US.
items.caveats: Leviton doesn't appear on IBEW-made or other union lists, and much of its production happens in Mexico and China. Its union status either way hasn't been confirmed.

items.name: Pella windows and doors
items.what: Pella makes windows and doors in Pella, Iowa and other US plants.
items.caveats: The company is family owned and non-union. Its heavy Made in USA marketing leads a lot of buyers to assume it's union when it isn't.

items.name: Andersen windows (Bayport MN, Menomonie WI) and Renewal by Andersen
items.what: Andersen makes its 100, 200, 400 and A-Series windows, along with Renewal by Andersen replacement windows, at plants in Bayport, Minnesota and Menomonie, Wisconsin.
items.union: None at window plants (only the EMCO storm-door plant in Des Moines is UAW)
items.caveats: Andersen is employee owned through an ESOP (employee stock ownership plan), but it isn't unionized. Don't confuse it with UAW-made storm doors from other manufacturers.

items.name: Marvin windows
items.what: Marvin makes windows at plants in Warroad, Minnesota and Fargo, North Dakota.
items.caveats: The company is family owned and non-union.

items.name: Lodge cast iron cookware
items.what: Lodge makes cast-iron skillets and Dutch ovens in South Pittsburg, Tennessee.
items.caveats: It's a beloved Made in USA brand, but the company is family owned and its workers aren't represented, so it doesn't appear on any union-made list. Lodge's enameled cast iron is made in China.

items.name: Vitamix blenders
items.what: Vitamix assembles its blenders in Olmsted Township, Ohio.
items.caveats: The company is family owned with no known union, and its motors and containers are partly imported. It doesn't appear on any union-made list.

items.name: Viking Range
items.what: Viking Range, owned by Middleby, makes its pro-style ranges and refrigeration in Greenwood, Mississippi.
items.caveats: These Mississippi plants are non-union, though the premium price and Made in USA label lead buyers to assume otherwise.

items.name: A. O. Smith / State / American water heaters
items.what: A.O. Smith, along with its State and American brands, makes residential water heaters in Ashland City, Tennessee, the world's largest water heater plant, plus Johnson City, Tennessee and McBee, South Carolina.
items.union: None known at Ashland City / McBee
items.caveats: A.O. Smith's old Kankakee, Illinois plant was union but has closed, and the current Tennessee and South Carolina plants aren't known to be represented. Bradford White is a UAW-made alternative if you want a union water heater.

items.name: Rheem / Ruud water heaters and HVAC
items.what: Rheem and Ruud water heaters are made in Montgomery, Alabama and Eagan, Minnesota, where the Marathon line is built, with HVAC equipment made in Fort Smith, Arkansas.
items.caveats: None of these plants appear on union-made lists, and the Montgomery and Fort Smith plants are believed to be non-union.

items.name: Goodman / Amana HVAC (Daikin) - Waller, Texas
items.what: Goodman and Amana-brand furnaces, air conditioners and heat pumps are built at the Daikin Texas Technology Park in Waller, Texas.
items.caveats: This Amana HVAC line is a Daikin brand and is a different company from the IAM-represented Amana refrigerator plant in Iowa, which people often confuse it with.

items.name: Electrolux / Frigidaire US plants (Anderson SC, Springfield TN, Kinston NC)
items.what: Frigidaire refrigerators and freezers are made in Anderson, South Carolina, ranges in Springfield, Tennessee, and dishwashers in Kinston, North Carolina.
items.caveats: Older union-made lists still show Frigidaire laundry appliances as IUE-CWA or UAW-made, but those plants have since closed. The Anderson, South Carolina plant announced more than 1,200 layoffs for 2026.

items.name: LG (Clarksville TN) and Samsung (Newberry SC) washers
items.what: LG has assembled washing machines in Clarksville, Tennessee and Samsung in Newberry, South Carolina since 2018.
items.caveats: Both plants are marketed as Made in USA, but neither is unionized.

items.name: Moen and Delta faucets
items.what: Moen, headquartered in North Olmsted, Ohio, assembles faucets at plants in New Bern and Sanford, North Carolina, and Delta Faucet assembles them in Greensburg, Indiana.
items.caveats: Neither brand appears on UAW, USW or IBEW union-made lists, and a large share of their production happens in Mexico and China. Kohler, made by UAW Local 833, is the union alternative.

items.name: Shaw and Mohawk carpet / flooring (Dalton, GA)
items.what: Shaw and Mohawk make carpet, LVT and laminate flooring in and around Dalton, Georgia.
items.caveats: The Dalton carpet industry as a whole is overwhelmingly non-union.

items.name: Ethan Allen furniture
items.what: Ethan Allen makes case goods and upholstered furniture at plants in Vermont, North Carolina and Mexico.
items.caveats: The company markets its North American manufacturing, but no union representation has been identified at any of its plants.

items.name: Master Lock padlocks (Milwaukee, UAW Local 469) - CLOSED
items.what: Master Lock combination padlocks used to be made by UAW Local 469 workers in Milwaukee, but that plant closed in 2024 and production moved to Mexico and Asia.
items.caveats: Older union-made lists, including from the Wisconsin AFL-CIO and the UAW guide, still show Master Lock, but it's no longer union-made.

items.name: Hy-Vee
items.what: Hy-Vee is an Iowa-based grocery chain with more than 285 stores across Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Missouri, Kansas, Nebraska and South Dakota, and it's expanding into Indiana, Tennessee, Kentucky and Alabama. It's been employee-owned through a trust since 1960.
items.caveats: The retail stores themselves are non-union, but Hy-Vee's distribution center in Chariton, Iowa, with about 500 warehouse workers and 200 tractor-trailer drivers serving more than 240 stores in eight states, is represented by Teamsters Local 238. Being employee-owned is often mistaken for being union, but Hy-Vee has no UFCW contracts and isn't on any UFCW-represented list. Union alternatives in its footprint include Cub, Lunds & Byerlys and Kowalski's in Minnesota, Jewel-Osco, Mariano's and Schnucks in Illinois, and Dillons, Baker's and Gerbes, all Kroger banners, in Kansas, Nebraska and Missouri.

items.name: Trader Joe's (all but 5 stores)
items.what: Trader Joe's has around 575 stores total, and only 5 are unionized: Hadley, Minneapolis, Louisville, Oakland and Chicago North Center. None of them has a contract yet.
items.caveats: The company has a progressive image, but it has been found to violate labor law during organizing campaigns.

items.name: Whole Foods Market (Amazon)
items.what: Whole Foods, owned by Amazon, has about 530 stores, and only one, the Philadelphia Spring Garden store, is unionized, with UFCW Local 1776 winning the election in 2025 but still no contract.
items.caveats: Amazon contested the Philadelphia election all the way through June 2026.

items.name: Costco (Minnesota, Illinois & most other warehouses)
items.what: Only about 56 of Costco's more than 600 US warehouses are Teamsters, located in California, New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Virginia and Washington. Midwest warehouses, including Minnesota and Illinois, are non-union.
items.caveats: Good pay and benefits, along with some union-made Kirkland items, lead people to assume Costco is union everywhere, but that isn't the case.

items.name: Target
items.what: Target, headquartered in Minneapolis, has no unionized stores anywhere in the US.
items.caveats: Because it's a hometown Minnesota brand, people often assume it's union, but it has historically been anti-union. That said, staff at its own naming-rights venues, like Target Field and Target Center, are union through UNITE HERE Local 17.

items.name: Starbucks (non-union stores; boycott)
items.what: About 9,000 Starbucks company-owned stores are non-union, and the roughly 500 stores that have unionized still have no contract. Workers United has called for a boycott and strike under the banner "No Contract, No Coffee."
items.union: none at most stores; SBWU asks customers to boycott
items.caveats: Even at a union store, the union is discouraging purchases until a first contract is reached.

items.name: Delta Air Lines (flight attendants, ramp, customer service)
items.what: Only about 20 percent of Delta employees are unionized, mainly pilots through ALPA and dispatchers. Flight attendants, who have an active AFA-CWA organizing campaign, ramp workers, who have an IAM campaign, and gate agents remain non-union, and Delta has actively resisted these organizing efforts.
items.caveats: Delta is the hub carrier at Minneapolis-St. Paul, so Minnesota flyers looking for a union airline should consider Sun Country, American, United, Southwest or Alaska instead. Note that Delta Sky Club and catering staff at MSP are UNITE HERE Local 17, even though Delta's flight crews aren't organized.

items.name: FedEx (Ground, Express, Freight)
items.what: FedEx Ground drivers are independent contractors or contractor employees rather than direct FedEx employees, and FedEx Express couriers are non-union under Railway Labor Act rules. Only FedEx pilots, represented by ALPA, are unionized.
items.caveats: Choose UPS or USPS instead if you want your package handled by union workers.

items.name: Amazon (delivery, warehouses, Whole Foods)
items.what: Amazon has no collective bargaining agreement anywhere in the US. It refuses to recognize the Teamsters-affiliated Amazon Labor Union at the JFK8 warehouse on Staten Island or its delivery driver units, and the Teamsters struck several Amazon facilities in December 2024.
items.caveats: Ship through UPS or USPS instead, and buy union-made goods directly from union retailers when you can.

items.name: T-Mobile US
items.what: T-Mobile has no CWA contract anywhere in the US, even though its parent company, Deutsche Telekom, is heavily unionized in Germany. CWA's T-Mobile Workers United campaign has been running since 2009 without ever winning a bargaining unit.
items.caveats: Switch to AT&T for a union carrier, since it's CWA represented, and Union Plus offers a discount on AT&T service.

items.name: Verizon Wireless retail (outside a few stores)
items.what: Verizon's wireless retail stores and call centers are non-union, except for the Brooklyn, New York store and the Everett and Lynnwood, Washington stores. The CWA and IBEW contracts cover the wireline Fios side in the Northeast, not wireless.
items.caveats: People often assume Verizon is union because of past wireline strikes, but the wireless business is a completely different story.

items.name: Most car dealerships (sales & service)
items.what: Outside of Chicagoland, where IAM Local 701 covers technicians, and parts of the Twin Cities, the Bay Area, Seattle, Boston and New York City, most dealership technicians are non-union, and sales staff are almost never union, even at dealerships that sell union-built vehicles.
items.caveats: Buying a UAW-built car from a non-union dealer still counts as buying a union-made car. For service work, though, look for an IAM or Teamsters shop specifically.

items.name: Skogen's Festival Foods (Wisconsin)
items.what: Festival Foods, run by Skogen's in Wisconsin, is non-union. It's easy to confuse with the similarly named Knowlan's Festival Foods in Minnesota, which is UFCW Local 663.
items.caveats: Wisconsin shoppers looking for a union grocery alternative can try Pick 'n Save or Metro Market, both Kroger banners represented by UFCW Local 1473.

items.name: Walmart / Sam's Club, Aldi, Lidl
items.what: None of Walmart, Sam's Club, Aldi or Lidl have any unionized stores in the US. Walmart is the largest non-union private employer in the country.
items.caveats: Aldi's German parent company is unionized in Europe, which sometimes causes confusion about its non-union US stores.
